Let's dive into the fascinating world of apples.As one of the most widely cultivated tree fruits in the world, apples (from the tree Malus domestica) have a deep history and incredible genetic diversity.The EssentialsOrigins: The wild ancestor of the domestic apple (Malus sieversii) originated in the mountains of Central Asia. Wild apple forests still exist today in Kazakhstan, where the former capital city's name, Alma-Ata, literally translates to \"Father of Apples.\"Diversity: There are over 7,500 known cultivars of apples worldwide. If you ate a different variety every day, it would take you more than 20 years to try them all.Genetics: Apples are \"extreme heterozygotes.\" If you plant a seed from a Honeycrisp, the resulting tree won't grow Honeycrisp apples—it will produce a completely new, unpredictable variety that is likely bitter like a crabapple. This is why commercial apple varieties are exclusively propagated by grafting branches onto existing rootstocks.Here's a look at some common varieties you might recognize at the grocery store or orchard: Popular apple varieties. Source: The Kitchn Find Your Perfect AppleBecause there are so many types, finding the right apple for a pie versus the perfect apple for a snack can be tricky.
